description: Evaluation incidents for the DevOps Incident Investigation Assistant. Written by the team, phrased as users would report problems. Never indexed (this folder is outside knowledge_base/). split=calibration questions are only used to tune thresholds; results are reported on split=test.

incidents.question: After we rolled out version 2.4 of our API, all the new pods restart every few minutes and kubectl get pods shows CrashLoopBackOff with a restart count above 20.
expected_causes: application error making the container exit
configuration error (environment variable, missing config file)
liveness or startup probe failing
not enough memory
expected_investigation_steps: kubectl describe pod to read Last State, reason and exit code
kubectl logs --previous to read the crashed instance logs
check what changed in the new version / rollback

incidents.question: My container starts, runs for about 30 seconds and then gets restarted. The events say the liveness probe failed. The app needs around a minute to warm up its cache.
expected_causes: liveness probe kills a slow-starting container
probe thresholds too short for startup time
expected_investigation_steps: read the probe events in kubectl describe pod

incidents.question: We pushed a new tag to our private registry, but the deployment's pods stay in ImagePullBackOff and never start. Other teams can pull public images fine.
expected_causes: wrong image name or tag
private registry without imagePullSecrets
pull secret missing in the pod's namespace or invalid credentials
expected_investigation_steps: kubectl describe pod and read the events
try docker pull of the exact image reference
check imagePullSecrets and the secret namespace

incidents.question: Our Java worker pod is killed regularly, the last state says OOMKilled with exit code 137, and memory usage grows slowly during the day before each kill.
expected_causes: container exceeds its memory limit
memory leak in the application
memory limit too low
expected_investigation_steps: kubectl describe pod for Last State OOMKilled and limits
kubectl top pod to see memory usage
check for a memory leak before raising the limit

incidents.question: I scaled a deployment from 3 to 10 replicas and four of the new pods have been Pending for an hour. The event says 0/5 nodes are available: insufficient cpu.
expected_causes: CPU requests do not fit on any node
cluster capacity exhausted
expected_investigation_steps: kubectl describe nodes to compare allocatable and allocated requests

incidents.question: A new pod for our GPU workload stays Pending; the scheduler message mentions that nodes had a taint the pod didn't tolerate.
expected_causes: node taint not tolerated by the pod
nodeSelector or affinity restricting nodes
expected_investigation_steps: check node taints and pod tolerations

incidents.question: Inside the cluster, curl to http://orders-svc returns connection refused even though the orders pods are Running. kubectl get endpointslices for the service shows no endpoints.
expected_causes: service selector does not match pod labels
pods not Ready (readiness probe failing)
wrong targetPort
expected_investigation_steps: call the pod IP directly on the container port

incidents.question: A service account used by our CI deploy job gets a forbidden error when it tries to create deployments in the staging namespace. How should the role and binding be set up?
expected_causes: missing Role/RoleBinding granting create on deployments
binding in the wrong namespace
expected_investigation_steps: check the Roles and RoleBindings of the namespace
verify which subject the binding applies to

incidents.question: After the security team applied network policies, our frontend pods can no longer reach the backend pods in the same namespace. Everything worked yesterday.
expected_causes: a default deny network policy blocks traffic
no policy allows ingress from the frontend to the backend
expected_investigation_steps: list the NetworkPolicies of the namespace
check which pods are selected and which ingress is allowed

incidents.question: We changed a value in a ConfigMap but the running application still uses the old setting. Do we need to restart something?
expected_causes: ConfigMap volume files are updated automatically but the application must reread them (no built-in signal)
values consumed at startup are not reloaded
expected_investigation_steps: check how the ConfigMap is consumed (environment variable or volume)
make the application reload its configuration or restart the pods

incidents.question: Our backend logs say it cannot resolve db.internal.example.com, but when I ping the IP address of the database directly it answers. This started after we moved the service to a new VM.
expected_causes: wrong or unreachable nameserver in /etc/resolv.conf
missing search domain
record does not exist in the zone
expected_investigation_steps: dig the name and read the status (NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL)

incidents.question: From a test pod, nslookup kubernetes.default fails and every service name times out, while IP addresses still work.
expected_causes: cluster DNS (CoreDNS) pods not running or failing
kube-dns service without endpoints

incidents.question: curl http://10.0.3.7:8080 fails immediately with connection refused, but ssh to the same machine works fine.
expected_causes: nothing listening on port 8080
service listens only on 127.0.0.1
service crashed or not started

incidents.question: Connections from the app server to the payment API on port 443 hang for two minutes and then fail with a timeout. Other external sites work.
expected_causes: firewall or security rule dropping packets
missing route
server overloaded
expected_investigation_steps: check firewall/security groups and routes along the path

incidents.question: Right after a deployment our nginx reverse proxy started returning 502 Bad Gateway for every request to /api, while the static pages still load.
expected_causes: backend not running or not listening on the expected port
backend closes connections
invalid response from upstream
expected_investigation_steps: call the backend directly bypassing the proxy
check the backend port after the deployment

incidents.question: Our report generation endpoint behind an AWS Application Load Balancer returns 504 Gateway Timeout when the report takes more than a minute to build.
expected_causes: target did not respond before the idle timeout
slow backend
expected_investigation_steps: compare with load balancer idle timeout

incidents.question: Since Monday our monitoring script fails with curl error 60 when calling https://intranet.corp.local, although the browser of my colleague shows the page.
expected_causes: certificate signed by a private CA not trusted by the client
expired certificate
incomplete chain

incidents.question: Browsers show NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID when users open our site through the load balancer DNS name.
expected_causes: hostname not covered by the certificate alternate names
default load balancer DNS name used
expected_investigation_steps: use the custom domain covered by the certificate

incidents.question: I run my image with docker run -d and the container disappears from docker ps within a second. docker ps -a shows Exited (0).
expected_causes: main process finishes (not a foreground process)
service started in background (service x start)
expected_investigation_steps: docker ps -a to read the exit code
check CMD/ENTRYPOINT runs in the foreground

incidents.question: docker run fails with exit code 127 and says the container command was not found or does not exist.
expected_causes: command missing from the image or misspelled
expected_investigation_steps: inspect the image entrypoint and cmd
run a shell in the image to check the binary

incidents.question: On a fresh Ubuntu server, docker ps works with sudo but as my normal user I get a permission denied error on /var/run/docker.sock.
expected_causes: user not in the docker group
group membership not reloaded
expected_investigation_steps: usermod -aG docker then log out/in or newgrp docker

incidents.question: docker info says Cannot connect to the Docker daemon. Is the docker daemon running on this host? I am working on my laptop and set up a remote engine last week.
expected_causes: DOCKER_HOST points to another host
daemon not running
remote host unreachable

incidents.question: I started my Flask container with -p 5000:5000 but http://server:5000 does not respond from my laptop, and even curl localhost:5000 on the host fails. Inside the container the app runs on 127.0.0.1.
expected_causes: application listening on 127.0.0.1 inside the container
wrong port mapping
expected_investigation_steps: docker port to check the mapping

incidents.question: My web container cannot connect to the database container using the hostname db. Both were started with plain docker run without any network option.
expected_causes: default bridge network has no automatic DNS between containers
expected_investigation_steps: create a user-defined bridge and attach both containers

incidents.question: PostgreSQL stopped accepting writes and the logs say No space left on device. df -h shows the root filesystem at 100%.
expected_causes: filesystem full (logs, data)
journal too large

incidents.question: I deleted a 20 GB log file to free space, but df still shows the disk as full.
expected_causes: deleted file still held open by a running process
expected_investigation_steps: restart the process holding the file

incidents.question: Our custom myapp.service fails right after start; systemctl status shows failed, and I edited the unit file this morning to add an EnvironmentFile.
expected_causes: EnvironmentFile missing or unreadable
unit file not reloaded with daemon-reload
wrong ExecStart path

incidents.question: After several quick crashes, systemd refuses to start my service again even though I fixed the config.
expected_causes: start rate limit reached (StartLimitBurst)

incidents.question: git push origin main is rejected with failed to push some refs; the message mentions non-fast-forward. A colleague pushed this morning.
expected_causes: remote branch contains commits not in the local branch
expected_investigation_steps: merge or pull then push again

incidents.question: On my new laptop every git clone over SSH from GitHub ends with Permission denied (publickey).
expected_causes: no SSH key loaded in the agent
public key not added to the GitHub account
wrong SSH user
expected_investigation_steps: ssh -vT to see which keys are tried

incidents.question: git merge stopped with CONFLICT (content) in two files and now I don't know how to finish the merge.
expected_causes: same lines changed in both branches
expected_investigation_steps: git status to see unmerged files
edit conflict markers, git add, then commit

incidents.question: After checking out an old commit to test something, git says I am in detached HEAD state and I made two commits there. How do I keep them?
expected_causes: commits made on a detached HEAD are not on any branch
expected_investigation_steps: create a branch from the current commit
use git reflog to find lost commits

incidents.question: Our GitHub Actions workflow that comments on pull requests fails with Resource not accessible by integration. We recently added a permissions block with contents: read to the workflow.
expected_causes: permissions not specified are set to none
GITHUB_TOKEN lacks pull-requests/issues write

incidents.question: The deploy step works on our branches but on pull requests coming from contributors' forks the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret is empty.
expected_causes: secrets are not passed to workflows triggered from forks
expected_investigation_steps: check the event that triggered the run
separate privileged steps from fork-triggered workflows

incidents.question: A workflow pushes a version bump commit using GITHUB_TOKEN, but our release workflow that listens to push events never starts afterwards.
expected_causes: events triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN do not create new workflow runs
expected_investigation_steps: use workflow_dispatch or a GitHub App token / PAT

incidents.question: Our GitLab job has been pending for 30 minutes and the job page says it is stuck. We have one project runner tagged docker.
expected_causes: job tags do not match any runner
runner does not run untagged jobs
expected_investigation_steps: compare job tags with runner tags
check the Run untagged jobs setting

incidents.question: In our GitLab pipeline the docker build step fails because the job cannot talk to the Docker daemon. The runner uses the shell executor on a VM.
expected_causes: gitlab-runner user not in the docker group
expected_investigation_steps: add gitlab-runner to the docker group

incidents.question: A CI variable with our deployment key is empty when the pipeline runs on a feature branch, but it works on main.
expected_causes: protected variable only available on protected branches or tags
expected_investigation_steps: list the variables in the job

incidents.question: terraform apply fails saying it cannot acquire the state lock. The previous pipeline run was cancelled in the middle of an apply yesterday.
expected_causes: stale lock left by an interrupted run
another run still holding the lock
expected_investigation_steps: check no other run is in progress
terraform force-unlock with the lock ID

incidents.question: Two engineers ran terraform plan at the same moment and one of them got a state lock error. Should we just disable locking with -lock=false?
expected_causes: concurrent run holds the lock

incidents.question: We moved our state from local files to an S3 bucket and now terraform init complains about the backend configuration having changed.
expected_causes: backend configuration changed requires -migrate-state or -reconfigure

incidents.question: terraform init on our Mac fails with Failed to install provider: the package doesn't match any of the checksums previously recorded in the dependency lock file. It works on the Linux CI.
expected_causes: lock file contains checksums for one platform only
expected_investigation_steps: terraform providers lock -platform for every platform

incidents.question: ansible all -m ping marks two of our new servers as unreachable, the others answer pong.
expected_causes: wrong remote user or SSH key
host key not known
network or SSH port unreachable

incidents.question: Our playbook with become: true just hangs on the first task that installs packages and never finishes.
expected_causes: stuck at the sudo password prompt

incidents.question: Ansible connects with SSH but modules fail because /usr/bin/python is not found on a minimal image.
expected_causes: Python interpreter missing or at another path

incidents.question: Our Lambda deployment script gets AccessDenied: user is not authorized to perform iam:PassRole. The same script works from my colleague's machine.
expected_causes: identity-based policy lacks the action
different credentials used on each machine

incidents.question: In our new sandbox account even an admin role gets is not authorized to perform because no service control policy allows the action.
expected_causes: implicit deny by a service control policy
expected_investigation_steps: review the SCPs with the organization administrator

incidents.question: I just launched an EC2 instance in a new subnet and ssh to its public IP times out.
expected_causes: security group without SSH rule from my IP
no route to an internet gateway
network ACL blocking
expected_investigation_steps: check route table and internet gateway
check network ACL including ephemeral ports

incidents.question: ssh -i mykey.pem to my Ubuntu EC2 instance prints a warning about an unprotected private key file and then Permission denied (publickey).
expected_causes: private key permissions too open
wrong username for the AMI

incidents.question: One of our EC2 instances stopped answering on every port and the console shows a failed system status check.
expected_causes: problem with the underlying AWS host requiring AWS involvement
expected_investigation_steps: stop and start an EBS-backed instance

incidents.question: Half of our users get errors since 10 minutes and I am the only one on call. Should I start by looking for the root cause in the logs?
expected_causes: major outage: mitigate before root cause
expected_investigation_steps: stop the bleeding (divert traffic, roll back)
pull in more people / declare an incident

incidents.question: Latency of our checkout service doubled this afternoon. What should I look at first to understand what is going on?
expected_causes: recent change (deployment or configuration)
saturation / overload
expected_investigation_steps: look at latency, traffic, errors and saturation

incidents.question: Several teams are debugging the same outage in parallel on different chat channels and nobody knows who is changing what. How should we organise ourselves?
expected_causes: unmanaged incident without clear roles

incidents.question: We rolled out a new deployment version and it is clearly broken. What is the fastest way to go back to the previous version while we investigate?
expected_causes: regression introduced by the new rollout

incidents.question: Containers on my Ubuntu desktop can't resolve our company's internal hostnames and docker prints a warning about a local 127.0.0.1 DNS resolver in resolv.conf.
expected_causes: host uses dnsmasq on loopback which containers cannot use

incidents.question: I ran git reset --hard by mistake and my last two commits are gone from the branch. Is there any way to get them back?
expected_causes: commits are no longer reachable from a branch but still exist
expected_investigation_steps: git reflog to find the lost commit
create a branch pointing to that commit

incidents.question: During node maintenance all replicas of our critical service were evicted at the same time and the service went down. How can we keep a minimum number of pods running during voluntary disruptions?
expected_causes: no PodDisruptionBudget defined for the application
expected_investigation_steps: define a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable or maxUnavailable

incidents.question: On our self-managed cluster, pods on the same node can talk to each other but pods on different nodes cannot reach each other at all.
expected_causes: pod network (CNI / multi-host networking) not working between nodes
expected_investigation_steps: check the CNI plugin and the multi-host networking setup
verify the Kubernetes networking requirements (pod-to-pod without NAT)

incidents.question: Our Kafka consumer group keeps rebalancing every few minutes and the lag grows. How do we fix it?
Our MongoDB replica set keeps electing a new primary several times per hour.
A long-running Oracle report fails with ORA-01555 snapshot too old.
After a driver update our Windows Server VM shows a blue screen with IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL at boot.
Our Elasticsearch cluster health turned red and several shards are unassigned.
